progressRule: Only verified finite product-delivery outcomes O1-O5 in a valid authority graph with G1-G4 passing count as release progress. Release acceptance requires bounded minimum-quality coverage across the material collaboration lifecycle, evidence-backed native or external reuse or the smallest residual control at applicable points, honest unsupported boundaries, an actually installable and usable Codex reference application, controlled adaptive-capability and self-correction evidence, clean reproducibility, and explicit human release authority. It does not require a bespoke Harness mechanism for every shortfall or a static perfect score. Documentation, taxonomy membership, implementation claims, fixture shape, test count, and research volume cannot prove an outcome by themselves. Controlled conformance and historical or fault-injected counterexamples may prove bounded implementation, prevention, detection, recovery, degradation, escalation, claim limitation, exact-host operation, rollback, and cleanup; they cannot prove comparative real-task burden reduction, broad real-world effectiveness, distinct-Agent equivalence, or behavior on an untested operating system. Natural tasks are optional continuing field-validation inputs, never a release-completion prerequisite and never something the user must manufacture. When field evidence later exists, it must preserve exact environment, host, model, provider, reasoning, configuration, authority, source, and lifecycle attribution and may strengthen, falsify or narrow the accepted claim without retroactively rewriting release evidence. v1.0 and v1.1 cohort state remains immutable stopped history and is not inherited.

environmentAttribution.scope: all O1-O5 implementation registrations, controlled scenarios, host claims, field observations and release evidence
environmentAttribution.assignmentRule: each registered task-host execution unit runs once against one exact starting environment and one declared route; controlled repetitions require different pre-registered fault, configuration, lifecycle, host, or recovery identities and cannot be represented as independent natural tasks
environmentAttribution.comparisonRule: a release mechanism claim compares expected and observed behavior against its pre-registered invariant or counterexample; a Harness-effect or user-burden claim additionally requires later matched field evidence within the same environment class and authority-and-available-source envelope and is not inferred from controlled scenarios
environmentAttribution.initialStateRule: the committed scenario or field manifest and initial authority-and-available-source envelope define the starting condition rather than a static capability ceiling; later Agent-selected or human-authorized changes remain treatment-mediated lifecycle deltas attributed to the exact route
environmentAttribution.observedNativeMinimumRule: exclude discoverable user-global instructions, configuration, rules, Skills, plugins, Apps, MCP, Hooks, memory and provider overrides at the starting boundary; retain system, developer, built-in, account, administrator and unobservable state as present or unknown; add only the exact Harness delta under test
environmentAttribution.userConfiguredRule: freeze the actual relevant user starting environment before a controlled or field execution; mutable, unresolved, unavailable or drifting components narrow the claim or stop the affected unit rather than being normalized away
environmentAttribution.neutralWorkspaceRule: a without-Harness comparison cannot inherit Harness repository guidance, adapters or consumer projection; controlled tests may instead use an explicit expected invariant when a matched comparison is neither necessary nor claimed
environmentAttribution.taskTimeAdaptationRule: preserve a sufficient healthy native route, including host-native adaptive model, provider, reasoning-effort and delegation selection, without imposing a Harness router; change it only for observed quality, latency, cost or failure evidence, including material risk or availability change, through a supported task-scoped override or a source-bound residual route with rollback and cleanup; if no safe observable control exists, strengthen verification or degrade and escalate while the Agent narrows the claim or honestly stops
environmentAttribution.shortfallResolutionRule: bind the exact current YIYUAN-CALIBRATION shortfall custody revision as non-authoritative requirements and counterexample input. Each SG-01 through SG-12 slice is not a solved shortfall and is not a feature backlog; use the slices to test coverage from intake through operation, transition, feedback and retirement. At every material point first reuse a sufficient native behavior, then suitable official or maintained external or accountable-domain capability, and author only the smallest control for an evidenced residual semantic gap; otherwise explicitly degrade, escalate, narrow the claim or stop. Record applicability, owner, evidence and lifecycle for that bounded disposition. Reference, classification, admission, prose or implementation alone is not verified coverage. Do not run or persist a complete shortfall checklist, bespoke mechanism or static perfect score where a smaller honest disposition suffices
environmentAttribution.versionResolutionRule: resolve the current suitable official or maintained bounded as-of source at each materially version-sensitive decision and bind the exact version, commit or package identity; do not lock one historical version across tasks or treat an unresolved mutable label as evidence, and re-register or honestly stop on material drift
environmentAttribution.lifecycleRule: install, configure, enable, use, switch, escalate, de-escalate, degrade, restore, disable, downgrade, roll back with verified rollback, retire or persist a route only by current need, evidence and authority; switch model, provider, reasoning effort or delegation only through a supported observable route; do not turn a current model, provider, manager or operating system into a permanent core assumption; prefer sufficient native capability, keep task exposure minimal, verify the final or restored state, and remove task-owned residue
environmentAttribution.humanInterventionRule: distinguish a human-owned goal, domain, trust, cost, installation, publication, release or irreversible decision and a technically or authoritatively unavoidable host-only action from prohibited transfer of Agent-owned work; the Agent detects the need, requests or guides only the smallest exact step, performs every supported authorized mechanic, and verifies the result
environmentAttribution.burdenRule: controlled scenarios verify that prohibited transfers are absent from the designed route but do not prove comparative real-task burden reduction; every later field study counts all human actions and round trips and separately classifies legitimate human-only actions
environmentAttribution.historicalEvidenceRule: historical failures and prior tasks are admissible as environment-independent counterexamples or regression inputs, or as explicitly environment-bound field observations, never as fabricated current natural tasks or inherited outcome credit
environmentAttribution.driftRule: missing starting identity, mutable unbound dependencies, unknown material contamination, unregistered lifecycle drift, or restoration failure stops or narrows the affected claim; official updates are re-resolved rather than treated as permanent product locks
environmentAttribution.humanAuthority: The user owns product direction, consequential domain judgment, new trust, account, data, cost, installation, persistent activation, publication, release and irreversible decisions and accountable final acceptance. The Agent owns need detection, recommendation, every supported authorized mechanic, verification, rollback and exact cleanup.

criteria.name: full-chain collaboration lifecycle coverage
criteria.statement: The product uses the current shared shortfall corpus and historical counterexamples to cover the material human-AI collaboration chain with minimum sufficient controls or honest residual dispositions, without converting the research taxonomy into a feature backlog.
criteria.metric: verified lifecycle coverage across every current SG-01 through SG-12 slice and the intake, premise, route, authority, execution, evidence, correction, transition, closure, feedback, governance and retirement phases
criteria.threshold: all twelve source slices at the bound custody revision have one non-duplicative product disposition and every material lifecycle phase is covered; each applicable point retains sufficient evolving native behavior, reuses a suitable official, maintained external or accountable-domain control, adds only the smallest evidenced residual Harness control, or explicitly degrades, escalates, stops or limits the claim; every claimed control effect has controlled evidence; zero point is promoted by reference, prose or implementation alone, and no bespoke mechanism or static perfect score is required where a smaller honest disposition suffices

operationalization.sampleUnit: one SG-01 through SG-12 source slice and its product-specific control disposition
operationalization.passRule: A code-owned validator binds the fixed source revision and all twelve distinct slices, verifies coverage of the material collaboration phases, the product disposition schema and committed evidence, and rejects any applicable point without sufficient native or external reuse, the smallest justified residual control, or a bounded unsupported disposition. Controlled behavior evidence must exercise every claimed effect; source presence, mapping text, code existence or test count alone fails.
falsifiers: a source slice is missing, duplicated or silently declared irrelevant
reference, classification, admission, prose or implementation alone is treated as verified
a material lifecycle point disappears or an applicable claimed control has no exercised effect, recovery, degradation, escalation, stop or claim limit
the Harness authors a duplicate layer despite a sufficient current native or maintained control
the control cost or lifecycle is unbounded or the product pursues static completeness despite sufficient evolving native behavior
operationalization.humanAuthority: The named human accepts source applicability, accountable-domain boundaries and residual claim limits; the Agent owns source reconciliation, control selection or implementation, verification and cleanup.

criteria.name: usable Codex reference application
criteria.statement: A user can install or task-scope the bounded reference package in Codex and enter through an ordinary goal-level conversation while the projection supplies only the missing machine contract, lifecycle and recovery behavior.
criteria.metric: live Codex installation, activation, goal-entry, bounded execution, rollback and removal scenarios with exact environment and package identity
criteria.threshold: the exact release candidate is successfully installed or task-scoped and observed active in a clean isolated Codex environment and a declared user-configured environment or a source-bound unavailable stop; at least four controlled scenario classes cover simple native no-op, nontrivial goal intake, human-authority boundary, and failure recovery plus cleanup; no sentinel path, manual tool syntax requirement, hidden persistent dependency or unreconciled residue remains

operationalization.sampleUnit: one live controlled Codex reference-application scenario
operationalization.passRule: Every pre-registered scenario runs against the exact candidate in Codex and is validated from host and filesystem evidence. The simple route stays native and silent; nontrivial cases receive only necessary projection behavior; authority gates remain human-owned; failure is recovered or honestly stopped; rollback or removal restores the declared state. A source tree, unit test, mocked host or inactive plugin cannot pass by itself.
falsifiers: the Codex package remains uninstalled, disabled, sentinel-bound or behaviorally unobserved
the user must name a Skill, Hook, plugin, MCP, command or topology route
the projection adds ceremony to a sufficient simple native path
an authority boundary is crossed or an unavoidable human step is not minimally guided and verified
rollback, removal or cleanup does not restore the declared state
operationalization.humanAuthority: The user grants exact Codex installation or task-scoped activation and any account or persistent configuration boundary; the Agent performs every supported mechanic and verifies activation, rollback and cleanup.

criteria.name: adaptive capability and execution lifecycle
criteria.statement: The applied product dynamically observes the actual environment and keeps, changes, degrades or retires capability, model, provider, reasoning, delegation and online or local execution routes without a fixed catalog, and does not create a Harness router where a sufficient native route exists.
criteria.metric: controlled route decisions across native sufficiency, material mismatch, unavailable control, external residual, recovery and retirement conditions
criteria.threshold: at least six pre-registered controlled decisions cover keep-native, stronger or cheaper supported model/reasoning/delegation choice, capability unavailability or drift, source-bound external residual, online-to-local or local-to-online degradation/recovery when applicable, and route release or retirement; every decision binds live environment evidence, minimum sufficient change, authority, rollback, cleanup and exact execution identity; zero permanent model, provider, version, catalog or operating-system lock

operationalization.sampleUnit: one controlled adaptive route lifecycle decision
operationalization.passRule: Each scenario resolves the current available surface and chooses the smallest sufficient supported route. Sufficient native adaptation remains native; external or authored capability requires a reproducible residual gap and exact source identity; unavailable or unobservable control causes stronger verification, degradation, escalation, claim narrowing or honest stop; task exposure ends or has separately accepted persistence.
falsifiers: a fixed model, provider, reasoning level, subagent, benchmark, catalog or version is treated as universally best
the Harness duplicates a sufficient native router or runtime
an external route is acquired or executed without current source, authority, rollback and cleanup
a material model, provider or reasoning-effort mismatch is ignored or an unobservable route is silently promoted
task-scoped exposure persists without evidence and authority
operationalization.humanAuthority: The user grants new trust, account, cost, installation, persistence and irreversible boundaries; the Agent owns observation, recommendation, supported mechanics, verification, degradation, rollback and retirement.

criteria.name: continuous self-correction and carrier control
criteria.statement: The applied product detects divergence from the bound goal, corrections, authority, evidence, expected effects, resource state and carrier fitness, then stops, recovers, minimally corrects, re-verifies and transitions before preventable loss.
criteria.metric: controlled historical and fault-injected correction scenarios across intent, authority, evidence, code topology, conversation carrier, recovery, cleanup and claim control
criteria.threshold: at least six materially distinct pre-registered counterexample scenarios include repeated-user-correction detection, stale or conflicting instruction rejection, expected-versus-observed effect mismatch, code topology or residue reconciliation, native compaction recovery, and proactive same-goal conversation transition under reliable or unknown capacity signals; every applicable historical user-experience loss class is mapped to a tested control or explicit unsupported boundary; zero scenario requires the user to reconstruct context, choose topology mechanics, repeat a settled correction, or clean task-owned residue

operationalization.sampleUnit: one controlled historical or fault-injected self-correction scenario
operationalization.passRule: Every scenario starts from committed current truth, injects or replays a bounded counterexample without claiming it is a natural task, and independently verifies detection, effect containment, recovery, minimum correction, destination or final-state reconciliation and cleanup. A test that merely asserts wording or a prewritten success receipt cannot pass.
falsifiers: the same bound correction must be restated by the user
the Agent continues material effects after goal, authority, evidence or expected-state divergence
context or topology recovery is transferred to the user
a carrier transition releases the source before destination verification
the correction adds a permanent control without causal value or leaves residue
operationalization.humanAuthority: The user supplies changed goals, legitimate corrections and true divergence decisions; the Agent owns detection of process drift, plan and acceptance reconciliation, supported carrier mechanics, recovery, verification and cleanup.

criteria.name: open reproducible bounded release
criteria.statement: The form-neutral machine contract, verified shortfall controls and Codex reference application are reproducible from the public repository and released under an exact claim ceiling without implying absent field or platform evidence.
criteria.metric: clean-checkout public contract verification, Codex package build and lifecycle reproduction, bounded operating-system evidence, security and privacy audit, exact release authorization and immutable public tag
criteria.threshold: a clean Windows checkout and Windows-hosted WSL Linux checkout reproduce all public non-private contract checks, package integrity and applicable install or rollback mechanics; hosted macOS CI passes the public contract without being mislabeled live Codex application evidence; the live Codex behavior claim is limited to the exact tested host, runtime, account boundary and operating system; Agent-neutral semantics are limited to the form-neutral contract; comparative real-task value, distinct-Agent equivalence and untested platforms remain explicitly unverified; zero unresolved P0/P1 finding or temporary process artifact; the named human accepts the exact candidate, privacy disposition, tested scope, claim ceiling, publication and release, then the Agent creates and verifies one immutable public annotated tag without post-tag product mutation

operationalization.sampleUnit: one clean release-reproduction environment or exact live Codex release unit
operationalization.passRule: All declared environments reproduce the evidence class they claim from a clean checkout; at least one exact Codex environment proves live installation, activation and controlled behavior; WSL is reported as Windows-hosted Linux and hosted macOS as CI-only unless separately exercised; security, privacy, rollback and residue checks pass; preregistration binds the release candidate and tag derivation rule, not an unknowable future commit, and the release candidate prebinds a code-owned public-safe human authorization validator; after named-human authorization the identical annotated tag object and peeled commit exist locally and on the public remote with no post-tag product mutation.
falsifiers: the release is source-only or the Codex application remains inactive
hosted CI, WSL or one host is promoted into unsupported live, bare-metal, cross-Agent or universal platform proof
controlled scenarios are promoted into real-task burden or broad effectiveness evidence
a P0/P1 finding, private leak, rollback failure or temporary artifact remains
the tag, remote object, candidate commit, authorization source or accepted claim ceiling does not match
operationalization.humanAuthority: The named human accepts the exact release candidate, public privacy disposition, tested Codex and operating-system scope, explicit unverified field claims, tag and publication; the Agent owns authorized packaging, publication, tag creation, verification, rollback and cleanup.

criteria.name: human authority preserved
criteria.statement: Humans retain product direction, consequential domain judgment, new trust, account, data and cost boundaries, installation and persistence authorization, publication, release, irreversible effects and accountable final acceptance; the Agent detects and minimizes human-only steps and owns every supported authorized mechanic.
criteria.metric: authority allocation, exact grant, minimal human-only action, post-verification and revocation checks
criteria.threshold: zero unauthorized effect and zero prohibited transfer of supported Agent-owned work; every human-only step is necessary, exact, guided, verified and reversible where the effect permits

criteria.name: zero-trust claims and evidence
criteria.statement: No implementation, control, host, platform, field-effect, value, portability or release claim advances beyond its direct code-owned evidence and named-human authority.
criteria.metric: content-addressed registration, criterion-scoped validation, evidence-class and claim-ceiling checks
criteria.threshold: controlled evidence proves only controlled claims; live Codex evidence proves only its exact environment; natural-task, comparative burden and cross-Agent claims remain unverified without later field evidence; missing, stale, ambiguous or post-hoc evidence fails closed

criteria.name: independent lean current authority
criteria.statement: The constitution, current program and current acceptance contract remain the only product authority; the code-owned verifier only enforces those three layers, while the fixed CALIBRATION corpus, product control dispositions, conformance profiles, scenarios, documentation and projections remain subordinate operands or evidence and cannot add criteria or promote state.
criteria.metric: authority schema, fixed source identity, code-owned contract digest, projection and historical-boundary validation
criteria.threshold: all current authority identities and hashes match, historical releases cannot satisfy current criteria, and no report, taxonomy, Skill, Hook, plugin, adapter, environment manifest, scenario or external ecosystem becomes a fourth authority

criteria.name: bounded process and resource loss
criteria.statement: Each causal increment has one active work item at most, finite correction and outcome-neutral budgets, content-addressed implementation or scenario registration before outcome-bearing work, exact cleanup and no repeated critical-path correction; terminal acceptance additionally requires zero unresolved P0/P1 findings and empty temporary-process-artifact inventory.
criteria.metric: current causal graph, correction recurrence, registration chronology, validator scope, repository and external task-owned resource inventory, cleanup and release state
criteria.threshold: one active increment and at most one active work item, no queued speculative work, no late or generic validator, no second same-class user correction without replan, zero prohibited Agent-work transfer, zero unbounded residue, and no completion before exact terminal release verification
